method: Original clinical cases; targeted primary/institutional retrieval supports selected premises. References are further reading, not blanket individual clinical validation. Medical facts were paraphrased; no official or proprietary test-bank questions were copied.
limitations: Not qualified clinical review or psychometric validation.
All sources were identified via retrieval; some were assessed from search excerpts rather than full-page retrieval.
A linked chapter may support the broad principle without validating every distractor.
International references support general clinical principles, not Canadian provincial authority.

targetedChecks.claim: Enzyme delivery with meals is supported; the case asks a focused use assessment.
Early and late symptom timing and delayed hypoglycaemia were checked.
Symptom-directed drainage is an available treatment option.
Bag and tubing are retained/returned when required under institutional reaction procedures.
Congestion pattern and delayed haemolysis features were checked in the Canadian guide.
Individualized stretching/splinting and addressing exercise-limiting pain are supported.
Acute pain/neurological warning pattern and urgent assessment are supported.
Prescribed weights should hang freely; position and alignment matter.
Symptomatic glucose1.7mmol/L at6hours requires immediate treatment, not routine feeding surveillance.
Intermittent distress/pallor/vomiting may be important despite well intervals.
Feeding/hydration support, gentle nasal suction and discharge clinical recovery criteria were checked.
Minimal agitation, fatigue/poor-air-entry severity, transient epinephrine effect and dangerous drooling differential were checked.
Worsening headache/vomiting/consciousness after initial improvement are cerebral-injury warnings.
